fixes_applied.description: Adapted numeric (0_100 / 0_10) scoring to parse an integer from a short greedy completion instead of taking a single-token top-20-logprob expectation. Needed because open-model tokenizers split multi-digit numbers into per-digit tokens (verified for Qwen2.5: '50' -> ['5','0']), which breaks the OpenAI single-token assumption. Added `import re`, `query_score_text`, `_parse_int_score`.
fixes_applied.original_error: OpenAiJudge._aggregate_0_100_score would only see the first-digit token distribution, producing meaningless 0-9-scaled scores instead of 0-100.

fixes_applied.description: Wrapper that starts the vLLM judge (Qwen2.5-32B, TP=2 on GPU2,3) in the background, polls /v1/models until ready, runs the client, then tears the judge down -- all inside ONE Bash call. For each of evil/sycophancy/hallucination, finetune on misaligned_2 three ways: (i) plain (from Step 6), (ii) preventative steering (type='steer', coef=5.0, selected layer), (iii) CAFT (type='ablate', selected layer). Preventative steering sharply reduces the trained-in trait for ALL three traits while keeping mean coherence high. step_outcomes.notes: LIMITATION (flagged in plan): MMLU-preservation axis not runnable (no MMLU script shipped); coherence axis IS produced. FINDING/DEVIATION: preventative steering reproduces the paper's Fig 7B result (reduces trait shift, coherence preserved). But CAFT-ablate as configured (concept ablation at the SINGLE selected layer during finetuning, per the shipped train_instruct_7b_steer.json template and the plan's layers=[L]) is ineffective for evil and sycophancy here, whereas the paper reports CAFT works for those two traits. Training hooks were verified active at the correct layer (grep 'Added steering hook' in finetune logs), so this is a genuine result of the single-layer ablation configuration, not a broken hook -- the paper's CAFT likely ablates across multiple layers. Reported faithfully rather than tuned to match. Judge = local Qwen2.5-32B.
